goal: Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers how a Granite UI dialog becomes a persistence contract, how relative field names write properties through Sling POST, and how to preserve authoring and rendering behavior across validation, legacy and empty states.

deck_context.source_summary: Class 8 of a seven-week AEM Sites course, delivered Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The audience understands Resources, Sling resolution, editable templates and content policies. This class traces component authoring from dialog definition through stored content and prepares developers to review the field-to-browser path used by later component work.
deck_context.core_claim: A safe dialog change treats the field name and stored value shape as a durable content contract, keeps dialog definition separate from authored Resources, and designs runtime behavior for configured, legacy and empty content.
canonical_facts: A project component definition is a cq:Component below /apps and can contain a cq:dialog child.
cq:dialog is an nt:unstructured Resource tree rendered server-side from sling:resourceType-driven Granite UI components.
An authored component instance lives below /content, stores content properties and retains a sling:resourceType that selects rendering capability.
A field named ./title addresses a title property relative to the Resource targeted by the form submission.
Sling POST can use @TypeHint control parameters when a specific JCR property type or multi-value shape is required.
Renaming a dialog field does not migrate properties already stored on existing component instances.
Granite UI validation improves authoring feedback but runtime code must still handle content created by older dialogs, packages, APIs or other tooling.
An empty component should remain visible and selectable to authors through an edit or preview placeholder while visitor output remains safe.

slides.title: A field change can become a content migration.
slides.intent: Show why renaming or reshaping a field affects content that already exists.
key_points: Existing instances retain properties written by the old dialog
Changing ./title to ./heading does not rename stored title properties
Reading only heading makes legacy instances appear empty
Read new, fall back to legacy, migrate, verify, then retire fallback
Changing property shape requires the same explicit decision

slides.title: Validation guides authors but does not guarantee stored content.
slides.intent: Distinguish helpful dialog constraints from runtime validation and compatibility responsibilities.
key_points: required, maxlength, emptyText and validators improve authoring feedback
Labels and descriptions explain intent and expected format
Existing, packaged or API-created content may bypass the current dialog
Model and rendering code handle missing, malformed or legacy values
Stored content is input, not proof that current validation ran

local_context.required_background: Authoring gate example: Title field has required = true, maxlength = 80, emptyText = Enter a concise title and a named validator. Runtime inputs include current valid content, a legacy title, missing title and an overlong packaged value. Show that dialog validation reduces preventable errors but does not sanitize repository history.

layout.composition: Two sequential gates: authoring guidance filters new dialog input, then runtime resilience evaluates every stored state; bypass routes feed directly into runtime.
layout.intent: Show why client-side authoring rules and safe runtime handling solve different problems.
